title: GPU maintenance queue review and capacity impact brief
content:
Purpose:
Quick mid-week review of the GPU maintenance / repair queue, decisions taken in today's infra huddle, and the near-term impact on capacity across regions. This is an operational snapshot + recommended next steps for next week's capacity plan.

TL;DR Summary:
- Total items in maintenance queue: 38 items (down from 46 last week).
- Immediate impact: estimated 7.4% effective slot loss cluster-wide for the next 72 hours due to prioritized repairs and firmware rollbacks.
- Root causes concentrated: 45% NVLink/mesh errors (hardware), 30% PSU/thermal throttles, 15% firmware regressions after driver update, 10% logistics (missing replacement parts).
- Action taken: deprioritized low-priority bench rebuilds, accelerated accept/ship for hot-replacement SKUs in us-west1 and eu-west1, temporary rebalancing of prewarmed pools.

Queue snapshot (2026-06-11 09:30 PT):
- Total open tickets: 38
  - HW replace (critical): 12
  - Firmware/driver incidents: 8
  - Thermal/PSU: 7
  - Networking (NVLink/span): 9
  - Logistics / parts pending: 2
- Median MTTR observed: 28 hours (target 24h)
- Tickets assigned to field techs: 22
- Tickets awaiting parts: 6

Regional breakdown (slots impacted, rough):
- us-west1: 18 slots offline (4 racks) — mostly NVLink failures concentrated on racks r5-r8. Expected return to service: staggered over 36-60h depending on cross-region part sourcing.
- eu-west1: 10 slots offline (2 racks) — PSU replacements ongoing, field team ETA 24h.
- us-east1: 6 slots offline — firmware rollback in progress, expected +12h to stabilize.
- ap-south1: 4 slots offline — logistic delay for replacements, currently being backfilled with spare nodes from us-east1 prewarm pool.

Estimated capacity impact (customer-facing throughput):
- Peak 99th percentile latency may increase by ~12–18% for very long-context workloads in affected regions if routing policy not adjusted.
- For multi-region customers with routing policy set to latency-first, we recommend temporary policy shift to cost-first or fallback-region routed to eu-west1/us-east1 for 6–48h depending on region.

Decisions made in huddle:
1) Deprioritize non-customer-facing bench rebuilds for the week (owner: Jordan Chen, done by 2026-06-12 EOD).
2) Initiate expedited RMA for NVLink failure cohort (tickets linked JIRA:INF-2412) with vendor SLA exception request (owner: María Lopez, POC with vendor: Michael Tang).
3) Move two prewarm racks from us-east1 to ap-south1 as temporary backfill (owner: Ethan Cole — schedule window 2026-06-13 02:00–06:00 UTC).
4) Implement short-lived routing override: all hosted-api traffic in us-west1 to prefer eu-west1 for sequences >8k tokens (owner: Priya Nambiar + release-engineering).

Risks & open questions:
- If vendor part shipments slip >48h, we will exceed 10% effective capacity loss and may need to throttle non-critical workloads. Contingency: activate burst-to-dedicated policy for top-tier customers.
- Firmware rollback on us-east1 has a 2% risk of causing increased KV-cache churn (see JIRA:INF-2467). We should watch tail-error metrics for the next 24h.
- Cross-region data egress and cost: recommended to run cost burn analysis before shifting long-running GPU jobs to eu-west1. Quick calc attached in linked artifacts.

Standup transcript highlights (paraphrased):
- Maria: "We got vendor confirmation for expedited NVLink parts, but need manager approval for SLA override."
- Alexei: "Thermal sensors on rack r7 are flaky — I'm logging a deeper hardware test after replacement."
- Ethan: "I'll reassign two spare nodes from the low-priority pool to ap-south1 and update capacity planner."

Short-term operational checklist (concrete tasks):
- [ ] Jordan to pause bench rebuilds (J: confirm by EOD 6/12)
- [ ] María to create vendor SLA exception request (JIRA:INF-2412) and track approval (due 6/13)
- [ ] Ethan to coordinate node migration window and update prewarm inventories (due 6/13)
- [ ] Priya + Release Eng to publish routing override and rollback plan (announce on #infra-ops; window 6/13 02:00 UTC)
- [ ] SRE oncall to create a short-lived metric dashboard (tails + error rate + KV cache churn) for the affected clusters (due 6/12 morning)

Notes for next week
- Evaluate whether a quarterly NVLink health-check should be added to standard preventative maintenance (owner: Alexei Ivanov). Proposal due by 2026-06-25.
- Re-run capacity hedging simulation with current queue assumptions and vendor lead-time of 72h. Impact to committed SLOs to be presented in next infra review (Priya, 2026-06-18).

Appendix: quick log entries (for audit)
- 2026-06-11 08:12 PT — INF-2412 created: NVLink error cohort flagged from automated telemetry (cluster: us-west1).
- 2026-06-11 08:50 PT — field tech dispatched to us-west1 rack r6-r8.
- 2026-06-11 09:01 PT — prewarm pool check: 14 nodes available for migration.
- 2026-06-11 09:20 PT — Routing override draft posted to #infra-ops for 15m review.

If you're reading this and own any of the tasks above, please mark your name in the checklist and update ticket links. If you need an exception for customer-affecting changes, escalate to Priya or the oncall manager (Jordan).

End of brief.
